comment: Scoped to the directories a person picks files FROM, not to all of $HOME.
There are exactly two callers — useSkillBootstrap.ts and PluginHost.vue —
and both read a file the user has just chosen in a native picker. That is
Downloads, Documents and Desktop; it is not the whole home directory.
The previous scope was $HOME/** with a deny list for .ssh, .gnupg, .aws,
.config and Library. That list is macOS-shaped: Library covers the app data
directory on macOS, but on Linux it is $HOME/.local/share/<bundle>/ and on
Windows it is under $HOME/AppData — neither was denied, and both hold the
per-profile .stronghold snapshot, vault_salt.bin and the SQLite database.
So on those platforms any frontend code-execution primitive could read the
encrypted vault straight off disk and brute-force it offline at leisure.
Argon2id raises that cost; it does not prevent the exfiltration.
An allowlist of pick-from directories rather than a denylist of secrets:
a denylist has to enumerate every sensitive path that will ever exist,
and the ones it missed are exactly the finding.
